brl_wolves.description: The Bleak Worgs of Nightmare Vale have started trotting up the Deathknell road after dark. They have not bitten anyone in Brill yet, which Deathguard Rennick considers both a stroke of luck and a warning. If the pack is thinned now, the luck may last through the winter.
brl_wolves.accept_text: Take the west road down to the Vale. Eight worgs. Bring me the count, and I'll pretend I'm not worried. I hold this gate with eleven soldiers and a bad feeling, so any fewer teeth on that road is a favour to me.
brl_wolves.turn_in_text: Eight? Good. Brill sleeps lighter than it admits, and tonight it may sleep a little deeper. Take something from the crate. It isn't much, but it's what we've got, and I'd rather it went to someone who earned it.

brl_nightmare.description: Nobody has walked the lower road of Nightmare Vale since the worgs arrived. Rennick wants it walked from end to end and reported, because "something" is a poor basis for a patrol roster, and the guard is beginning to name the unknown things out there.
brl_nightmare.accept_text: South-west of the Cold Hearth road, past the Deathknell gate, the road goes into the trees. Walk it to the bottom. Don't dawdle, and don't take the shortcuts the worgs use. They're shorter for a reason.
brl_nightmare.turn_in_text: So it's quiet down there. I like quiet less than you'd think. Quiet means something has decided to wait. Good work. I'll put a watch on the road tonight, and I'd like you to stay inside the walls if you can.

brl_glades.description: The Wretched Zombies that wander the glades west of Brill have begun drifting toward the gate. They are slow and stupid and mean no harm, but the guard at the gate has a quota of corpses he is willing to step over, and he reached it on Tuesday.
brl_glades.accept_text: Out along the road west. Zombies, eight of them. Put them down and I'll let you back in without a lecture. And please try not to bring any back with you on your boots. It's happened before.
brl_glades.turn_in_text: That's the road clear. I was getting a crick from all the stepping over. Thanks. You've got a talent for this, you know. I mean that kindly. It's an ugly talent, but Brill needs it.

brl_news_landing.description: Wexley the crier prides himself on hearing everything first, and he has heard that the Undercity zeppelin tower east of Brill is now open to passengers. He has no way to confirm it, and the idea of announcing a false rumour keeps him from sleeping. He would very much like you to go and look.
brl_news_landing.accept_text: East along the high road, then south. The tower is a tangle of ropes and goblin curses, I'm told. Go and tell me if it's real. If it is, I shall cry it from the steps by noon. If it isn't, I'll never speak of this again.
brl_news_landing.turn_in_text: Real! Real, and open for custom. I shall cry it from the steps. Thank you! There is nothing so fine as a piece of news with a witness. I'll make you famous, if you like. A little famous. A whisper.

brl_news_ruins.description: The Landing is one thing. The Ruins of Lordaeron, just south, are another: the old capital, the gate to the Undercity, and a roosting place for every rumour the town crier cannot afford to miss. Wexley wants someone to walk the approach and see who is still home.
brl_news_ruins.accept_text: South of the landing, along the road the Dark Lady took. Don't linger. The ghosts remember being important, and they get touchy about it. Tell me who you see, and what they're wearing. I'll make a story of the rest.
brl_news_ruins.turn_in_text: The old throne's cold, then. Pity. It was a lovely rumour. Never mind. There's a new one every week, and the next will be better. Thank you. A crier who stops hearing things is only a man shouting.

brl_grael_pumpkins.description: Assistant Grael needs the pumpkins the Solliden thrashers have been growing: swollen, grey-green things that ferment into the Apothecary's best base for plague reagents. He will not go near them himself. The thrashers hit back, and Grael does not like being hit back.
brl_grael_pumpkins.accept_text: The Grain Threshers in the Solliden fields carry them. Five, uncracked, please. I'm very particular about cracks. A cracked pumpkin tastes of failure, and so does the batch it ruins.
brl_grael_pumpkins.turn_in_text: Perfectly foul. Look at the colour! It's practically glowing. Take something from the shelf, you've earned it. And if you happen to have a very strong stomach, I could use you again. I find I like working with people who don't flinch.

brl_grael_pearls.description: The Vile Fin oracles on Whispering Shore wear salt-pearls the Apothecary can grind into a calming powder. Grael has no idea what the Vile Fins want them for, and not much interest in the answer. He only knows that the powder works, and that supplies are low.
brl_grael_pearls.accept_text: North-west, where the bay meets the dead marsh. The little oracles. Five pearls, and don't scratch them. Scratched pearls make for jittery powder, and I will not be held responsible for what jittery powder does to a patient.
brl_grael_pearls.turn_in_text: Lovely lustre. Ground fine, these will keep a grave-robber asleep for a month. Take your pick from the shelf. You may find something you like. You may find several. I'll pretend I didn't notice.

brl_grael_iceshard.description: Brightwater Lake sheds shards of black ice no matter the weather, and the weeping shades that stalk its shore carry them like keepsakes. The Apothecary uses them for cold-fixing, and Grael is down to the last few slivers. He needs five.
brl_grael_iceshard.accept_text: Eastern Tirisfal, Brightwater Lake. The shades and the drowned wretches carry fragments. Bring five, and gloves. Wear gloves. The shards are older than Brill, and they bite.
brl_grael_iceshard.turn_in_text: Cold enough to hurt. Excellent. Your reward is on the third shelf. Do not touch the fourth. I mean it. I've had to scrape a man off the fourth shelf once, and I have no desire to repeat the experience.

brl_hollis_robbers.description: Gravedigger Hollis has dug graves for thirty years, living and dead, and he knows when one has been robbed. The Rot Hide gnolls up at Garren's Haunt are doing it, and they leave the bodies in the wrong places, laid out like stage props. He takes it as a personal insult.
brl_hollis_robbers.accept_text: The graverobbers use shovels. I recognise the shovels. They're mine. Six of them, and bring the shovels back. I don't mind the gnolls so much as I mind the carelessness.
brl_hollis_robbers.turn_in_text: Six less. I'd say rest in peace, but they never earned it. Take your pick. And thank you for the shovels. A gravedigger without his tools is only a man with opinions about dirt.

brl_hollis_relics.description: Whatever the robbers and the crypt wights took, Hollis wants it back in the ground where it belongs: rings, seals, small carved relics from the Agamand family vault. He has no interest in the value. A grave without its keepsakes is not finished, and he will not have an unfinished grave.
brl_hollis_relics.accept_text: The wights in the Agamand crypt and the robbers at Garren's Haunt carry the best of it. Five relics, and no keeping any. I'll know. The dead have a way of telling me.
brl_hollis_relics.turn_in_text: All present. I'll bury them tonight with a proper word. Take something from the barrow. I'd offer you a seat, but the only chair is one I dug. You wouldn't like it.

brl_meryl_orders.description: Meryl Ashdown has a brother in the Scarlet Crusade, and she has not heard from him in a year. She wants to know whether he is still alive, still sane, or still listed. Conversion orders from the Crusader Outpost might tell her. She will not ask what you do to get them, and she would like you not to tell her.
brl_meryl_orders.accept_text: The Crusader Outpost, west of the Solliden farms. The recruits carry their orders on them. Please. Five. And don't hurt him if you meet him. I don't know what he looks like any more, but he'll have my mother's chin.
brl_meryl_orders.turn_in_text: ...He's on the roster. Alive, at least. Thank you. I won't forget this. Take something. It was his, from before. I think he'd want a stranger to have it, if it meant I'd stopped crying.

brl_nettles_crows.description: Old Farmer Nettles swears the duskbats over the glades are the crows that used to eat his barley, and that they are still after it. Nothing has grown on his plot since the Plague, but he insists on the principle, and in fairness, it is a very good principle.
brl_nettles_crows.accept_text: Out in the glades, the big grey ones. They've had my crop and my patience. Eight of them, if you please. I'd do it myself, but they know my hat.
brl_nettles_crows.turn_in_text: Eight. I'll hang them on the fence. It's what you do. Take some of the old tack. It's not much, but it was Mildred's, and she'd want it used. Not in the barn, though. The barn's cursed.

brl_pruit_straw.description: Pruit tends the scarecrows that guard Brill's allotment plots. The Rotting Dead that stumble in from the glades keep knocking them down and, worse, leaving their own shapes standing on the posts, in the scarecrows' place. Pruit would like the posts back.
brl_pruit_straw.accept_text: The glades, west. Seven, and don't bring them back. I'll make do with straw. The scarecrows never complain. They never help, either, but they never complain.
brl_pruit_straw.turn_in_text: Straw's easier to stand up than they are. Thank you, friend. Take what you need. I'll mend the posts tonight, and if I get them right, nobody will notice there was ever a problem. That's what mending is for.

brl_ohmsted_toll.description: The bell-ringer rings once a day for those lost at Brightwater Lake. Lately the Drowned Wretches have started ringing back, a thin wet echo from the water, and it is putting the whole of Brill off its supper. Ohmsted wants them quiet, and wants his bell to be the only one in the valley.
brl_ohmsted_toll.accept_text: East past Brill, the big lake on the north side. They rise at dusk and wail. Seven, please. And don't stand under the bell tower on your way back. I've a feeling about that beam.
brl_ohmsted_toll.turn_in_text: Quieter, I think. Or I've gone deaf. Either way, thank you. I'll ring the evening bell and hear it properly. It's been so long since I heard my own sound.

brl_ohmsted_shades.description: The Weeping Shades answer the toll with their own. It is the worst sound in Tirisfal, a dripping, keening complaint that rises from the lake after the bell stops. Ohmsted would like them gone, or at least discouraged, so that the toll can be a toll and not a conversation.
brl_ohmsted_shades.accept_text: Same lake. The shades. They're rather high-handed about it. Six, if you can stomach it. They'll look at you as if you owed them something. You don't.
brl_ohmsted_shades.turn_in_text: I can hear the bell again. It's a lovely sound, if you're me. I'll tell the dead you did them a kindness. They won't believe me, but it's good to say it.

brl_joss_home.description: Farmhand Joss remembers a stable, a farmhouse and a woman who made bread. He thinks it was south of the Brill road, near an overgrown paddock. The rest of his life has gone, and he wants someone to walk the place and tell him whether it is still there, because he is afraid to look himself.
brl_joss_home.accept_text: Balnir, I think they called it. South of the east road. Look at the farmhouse for me and tell me what's left. You people remember where you came from, don't you? I'd give a great deal to be able to say the same.
brl_joss_home.turn_in_text: The stable's still standing? That's... something. Thank you. I'll remember it better now. Even a bit of a place is better than none. I think I'll go and sit in it, one day, and see if the bread comes back.

brl_ilvessa_cargo.description: Trader Ilvessa's shipment never made it from the Undercity zeppelin to her stall. Scavengers picked it clean on the road, and she wants her crates back before the next delivery arrives and the scavengers get ideas. She has already sent three letters to the Undercity about it, and has been told, politely, to hope.
brl_ilvessa_cargo.accept_text: Ragged scavengers along the Eastern road. They steal anything that glints, and I do mean anything. Six crates, please. I'd offer a reward, darling, but I'm still tallying what they took.
brl_ilvessa_cargo.turn_in_text: My goods! Mostly my goods. Take your cut, darling. It's a pleasure to do business with someone who can lift a crate and not ask questions. Come back if you need anything. My prices are fair, and my memory is long.

wtv_wolves.description: Ranger Corvin Ashe walks the edge of Nightmare Vale for the Deathguard, and the Bleak Worgs have been growing bolder. He needs the pack thinned before it learns to climb the road, and he does not have the arrows to do it alone.
wtv_wolves.accept_text: They hunt in the dusk. Eight should keep them wary. Aim for the grey ones, they lead. If you see a white one, leave it. I'm not sure what it is, and I'd rather it didn't know my face.
wtv_wolves.turn_in_text: That's quieter. Nobody ever thanks a ranger for what doesn't happen. I'm thanking you. It's an odd sort of sensation, being grateful. I'm not entirely sure I like it.

wtv_crawlers.description: Nightcrawlers burrow in the Vale's loam and snap at anyone who walks overhead. Corvin has lost two boots to them and more dignity than he cares to admit. He has been walking the Vale on tiptoe for a week.
wtv_crawlers.accept_text: Under the roots. You'll feel them before you see them. Seven, please, before they grow. A grown one would take my leg and leave me a sock.
wtv_crawlers.turn_in_text: Good. A man can walk again. Take a piece of the kit. And please, if you're ever in the Vale and you see me dancing, I'm not. I'm only checking the ground.

wtv_needler.description: A big old duskbat called Ressan the Needler nests above the Vale road: needle-sharp teeth, a taste for ankles, and a flock that follows him wherever he goes. Corvin has had enough of being the Vale's ankle.
wtv_needler.accept_text: He's a brute, flies low, and screams. Clear his flock and then him. I'll watch from here, with my boots on. I've decided, as a matter of principle, to keep them on.
wtv_needler.turn_in_text: He's down. I can hear myself think. Well done. Choose what suits you. If he had friends, they'll look for you, so keep your boots on too.

wt_manor_reapers.description: Watcher Pell has kept the Cold Hearth gate for a year, and the reapers have never stopped coming. They come up out of the manor cellars with scythes and no manners, and she cannot quite remember when she last had an uninterrupted watch.
wt_manor_reapers.accept_text: Eight, and be careful with the scythes. They've been sharpened since before you died. Or before I did. Honestly, I stopped counting. Just don't let them get behind you.
wt_manor_reapers.turn_in_text: Eight. That's the first quiet watch in a month. Take something from the pile. I'd say get some rest, but I've the feeling you won't.

wt_manor_dead.description: The reapers aren't the only thing in the hall. Zombies and Rotting Dead pour out of the grounds as if the manor were calling them home, and every night the garden gate is a little more crooked. Pell wants the grounds cleared before they come for the gate itself.
wt_manor_dead.accept_text: Clear the gardens. Zombies and the rotted ones. The sooner they stop coming, the sooner I stop watching. Six zombies, four rotting. If you find the gate lock, leave it. It's the only thing holding.
wt_manor_dead.turn_in_text: The gardens are empty. For now. Thank you. Your pick of the lot. And if you're ever bored, I'm told the manor's roof is a fine place to watch the sun go down. I don't recommend it, but it's a fine place.

wt_aldous.description: Reaper-Lord Aldous is what the manor's dead report to: a tall, scythe-armed wreck who still thinks the hall is his. Pell would very much like him to be wrong, and has begun, quietly, to prepare the case.
wt_aldous.accept_text: Inside the hall, at the hearth. His reapers will guard him. Take them first, then Aldous. And don't let him talk. He's very good at giving orders, and you've the look of someone who listens.
wt_aldous.turn_in_text: The Lord of the Hall, in pieces. I'll have the hearth lit again. Take what you want. And do me one favour: if you ever see a chair by the fire, don't sit in it. It's still his.

wts_puddlejumpers.description: Fisher Quillon's nets are in tatters and his boat is gone. The Vile Fin murlocs of Whispering Shore took the boat and use the nets as hats. He wants them put in their place, which, in Quillon's opinion, is somewhere farther from his boat.
wts_puddlejumpers.accept_text: Along the strand to the north-west. The little ones. Eight, and bring back my dignity if you find it. If you find my hat too. It's red.
wts_puddlejumpers.turn_in_text: That'll teach them. Probably not, but it'll teach me something. Take a piece of what's left. I'll bring the rest down to the bay myself, once the weather turns. The bay and I have an understanding.

wts_pearls.description: The oracles of Whispering Shore wear pearls to speak to the tide, and lately the tide has been speaking a great deal of nonsense. Quillon thinks taking the pearls might quiet it, or at least put a stop to the murlocs reading his mail.
wts_pearls.accept_text: The Minor Oracles carry them. Five pearls, and if the tide screams, run. I don't think it will. But I have a feeling about the tide, and the feeling is not good.
wts_pearls.turn_in_text: Quiet at last. Even the gulls have stopped. Your pick, friend. And thank you. A man gets used to the sea being cross with him, and then it's like a death when it stops.

wts_gillrot.description: Old Gillrot leads the Vile Fins, a withered oracle with a staff made from a drowned man's mast. He is the one who stole the boat. Quillon wants it back, and wants him made to understand that a boat, even a rotten one, is not a gift.
wts_gillrot.accept_text: He sits on the biggest rock. His oracles heal him, so thin them first, then Gillrot. Don't mention the boat to him. He gets sentimental, and then he gets violent.
wts_gillrot.turn_in_text: My boat's still rotten, but it's mine. Take whatever you like from his trove. Not the staff. I'd like the staff. It's the mast of my cousin's boat, and I'd rather see it on land.

wto_converts.description: Scout Dessa Vane watches the Crusader Outpost from the thorn-line. New recruits arrive weekly, wide-eyed and fanatical, and the Deathguard would like fewer of them to reach full conviction. Dessa has been counting them for a month and the number only goes one way.
wto_converts.accept_text: They're green and enthusiastic. That makes them dangerous. Eight, and keep to the shadows. They sing hymns when they march. If you hear singing, don't answer.
wto_converts.turn_in_text: Fewer recruits, fewer problems. The Crusade bleeds. Pick whatever you can use. I've got a notebook, and I'll put your name in it, if you'd like. It's the only thing I've got that doesn't rot.

wto_initiates.description: Behind the converts stand the Initiates: trained, armed and devout. They carry the Crusade's banners and the outpost's stubbornness, and Dessa has watched them drill on the parade ground until her eyes ache. She wants them cut down before they march on Brill.
wto_initiates.accept_text: They're better than the converts. Don't take more than two at once. Six, please. And if they offer to convert you, say no politely. They're not good at hearing no.
wto_initiates.turn_in_text: A good cut. I'd say the Crusade will feel that. Take what you can carry. And watch the road home. The ones you missed will be out for revenge, and they sing while they plan it.

wto_korgal.description: Meven Korgal commands the Crusader Outpost: a veteran, a zealot and an excellent shot with a prayer. If he falls, the outpost will fall with him, and Dessa has been waiting a long time for someone to try.
wto_korgal.accept_text: He's at the heart of the camp. His recruits will rally, so thin them first, then him. He prays before every shot. If you're quick, you'll have finished before he's finished the first line.
wto_korgal.turn_in_text: Korgal's dead. The camp's a rabble. That'll buy Brill a season. Have your choice of the lot. I'll tell Rennick it was you. He pretends he doesn't care, but he'll write it down.

wtf_farmhands.description: Widow Marren's farmhands stayed on after the master died, and after they died. They work the fields at all hours with rusted tools and no direction, and she cannot bring herself to chase them off. She asks that you put them down gently, if it can be done gently at all.
wtf_farmhands.accept_text: They don't know any better. Put them down gently. They were good men. They'd been with the farm since before I married. Eight of them, and please, close their eyes after.
wtf_farmhands.turn_in_text: Thank you. I'll sit with the ones who remain. Please, take something. It's not much. It was my husband's. I'd like you to have it, and I'd like it not to come back.

wtf_threshers.description: The Blighted Grain Threshers, machines that run themselves, have eaten the last of the harvest and are looking for more. They do not seem to know what a harvest is any more. Marren cannot stop them, and they are slowly working their way toward the house.
wtf_threshers.accept_text: They're iron and rot. Seven of them, before they find the house. I've done what I can with the barn door. It won't hold forever.
wtf_threshers.turn_in_text: The fields are quiet. Still ruined, but quiet. Take some of the old tack. I'll sit on the porch and listen to nothing. It will be the first time in weeks.

wtf_goodman.description: Her husband, Goodman Solliden, walks the fields with a pitchfork and a blighted grin. Marren wants him laid to rest, and does not want to watch. She has left a lamp in the window every night, and every night he has walked past it without a glance.
wtf_goodman.accept_text: He's out among the pumpkins. His men will guard him. Be kind to him, if you can. He used to sing to the cows. I'd give a great deal to hear it again.
wtf_goodman.turn_in_text: ...Thank you. He was a good man once. Take his things. I can't look at them. I'll take down the lamp tonight. It's time.

wtp_lurkers.description: Hermit Oswin lives by Stillwater Pond because no one else will. The crab-like lurkers in the silt are the only neighbours he has, and they bite. He has grown fond of the sound they make when they scuttle, but not of the bite.
wtp_lurkers.accept_text: They hide in the mud and pinch. Eight, and watch your ankles. Mine are already scarred, and I'd rather not lose the other one.
wtp_lurkers.turn_in_text: Fewer pincers. A man can wash his feet again. Thanks. If you ever need directions through the swamp, ask me. I know three paths, and only one of them goes where it says.

wtp_dead.description: The Rotting Dead shuffle out of Stillwater Pond at all hours, singing a hymn no one remembers. Oswin finds it unrestful, mostly because it is nearly familiar, and he cannot place it. He has stopped trying, and the hymn has not stopped.
wtp_dead.accept_text: They hum. I can't stand the humming. Seven, please. And if you hear the words, try not to remember them. I don't want to be the only one.
wtp_dead.turn_in_text: Silence at last. I think I'll sleep. Choose well. I'll have a quiet night, and perhaps a quiet week. I haven't had one of those since the bell.

wtp_murk.description: Something large sits at the bottom of Stillwater Pond. Oswin calls it Murk. It bloats with every drowned thing and belches them back up on the shore, and he has begun to suspect it is keeping count.
wtp_murk.accept_text: It comes up when you splash. Clear the lurkers, then call it out. Don't fight in the water. The water is on its side. The bank is on yours.
wtp_murk.turn_in_text: The pond's clear. Well, clearer. Take his treasures. I've no use for them. I only wanted the silence, and now I've got it, I'm not certain what to do with it.

wta_servants.description: Envoy Sorren speaks for Brill at the old Agamand mill. The Agamand servants still tend the house they died in, and they will murder anyone who tries to take the grain. Sorren needs the mill's stores for Brill's winter, and the servants have not noticed the war ended.
wta_servants.accept_text: They're stubborn, not smart. Eight, and don't let them corner you in the mill-race. The wheel's slippery, and the servants will use that to their advantage. They know the house better than you.
wta_servants.turn_in_text: That'll thin the household. Sorren thanks you. Take your pick. And when you next pass the mill, don't wave at the windows. They wave back.

wta_keys.description: Captured farmers are held in the mill cellars, shackled and slowly rotting. The servants carry the keys, and nobody has dared take them. Sorren wants the captives freed, or at least unlocked, so that someone can finally decide what to do with them.
wta_keys.accept_text: The servants have the keys on them. Three should open the lot. Bring them to me. And don't open any door that's already open. You'll know why when you see it.
wta_keys.turn_in_text: Three keys. That's freedom for the lot of them. Take something for the trouble. They'll be grateful, though not for long, and not in any way that will make sense to us.

wta_thurman.description: Thurman Agamand was the miller, then the lord, then something worse. He reigns in the mill-house with a family of ghouls at his heel. Sorren wants the house back, and wants the grinding to stop, because the sound carries all the way to Brill.
wta_thurman.accept_text: He's at the heart of the mill. His ghouls come first. Be ready. He's got a way of talking that makes you want to be his friend. Don't be.
wta_thurman.turn_in_text: The mill's ours. The Agamands are dust. Take what you like from the strongbox. And wash the flour off your boots before you come into Brill. It has a way of getting into things.

wtc_wights.description: Keeper Halvard guards the Agamand crypt gate and has not been inside since the wights woke. They hold the vaults now, and he has listened to them stir for a month. He wants them cleared, because the crypt gate has started to creak outward.
wtc_wights.accept_text: They're strong, hungry and old. Eight, and don't let them gang up. If one calls you by name, keep walking. I don't know who they think you are, but they're always very pleased.
wtc_wights.turn_in_text: That's the vaults breathing easier. Thank you. Take something. I'll light a candle at the gate. It's an old habit, and I don't plan to break it.

wtc_dargol.description: Captain Dargol, last of the Agamand guard, rose to defend a family that is already dust. He fights anything that comes near the dead, with great discipline and no hope, and Halvard cannot decide whether to admire or pity him.
wtc_dargol.accept_text: He's at the deepest vault. His wights guard the door. Clear them, then him. He'll salute you, first. I'd salute back. It costs nothing, and it's the last thing he'll ever get.
wtc_dargol.turn_in_text: Dargol's at rest. The vault is ours. Take your pick of the old arms. They were good steel, once. I hope they will be again.

wth_mongrels.description: Warden Brask holds the line at Garren's Haunt, and the Rot Hide mongrels that follow the gnolls have turned the fields around it into a kennel. They are mangy, starved, and not at all afraid, and Brask has stopped sleeping with his boots off.
wth_mongrels.accept_text: They come in packs, mangy and starved. Eight, please. If one's wearing a collar, it was somebody's once. Don't think about that.
wth_mongrels.turn_in_text: That's the field quiet. Take a piece of the kit. I'll keep the fire going. It's all I can do, and it's something.

wth_gnolls.description: Behind the mongrels stand the Rot Hide gnolls: brutes in stitched hide with clubs as long as your arm. They dig up graves for fun, and Brask has found three this month that were empty. He is not amused, and he has started writing names on the stones.
wth_gnolls.accept_text: They have clubs and bad tempers. Seven should get the message across. And if they laugh, don't take it personally. It's how they breathe.
wth_gnolls.turn_in_text: Seven fewer clubs. Excellent. Your pick. I'll tell Hollis you did him a kindness. He'll pretend not to care and then he'll bring you a loaf.

wth_maggot.description: Maggot Eye is the gnoll chieftain: scarred, rotted, and bigger than the rest. His tribe follows him because he bites harder than they do, and because he has never once been seen to hesitate. Brask wants him gone, and the tribe leaderless.
wth_maggot.accept_text: He sits in the middle of the camp. His guards come first. Be quick. He's got one good eye and he uses it, so stay out of the middle.
wth_maggot.turn_in_text: Maggot Eye's gone. The tribe will scatter. Take your pick of the camp's loot. And be careful where you sleep tonight. Scattered tribes don't always leave.

etl_dusk.description: Deathguard Linnea keeps order at the zeppelin landing. Duskbats roost in the ropes and drop on passengers, which is, she says, bad for business, worse for the passengers, and not at all good for her reputation among the goblins.
etl_dusk.accept_text: Up in the ropes and along the road. Eight, please, before the next boat. If you hit a rope, tell the goblins it was an accident. They're sensitive about the ropes.
etl_dusk.turn_in_text: The landing is quieter. Thank you. Take something from the supply crate. I'll make sure the next passenger knows who to thank, even if they never ask.

etl_dead.description: Zombies wander the road between Brill and the landing, blocking carts. They are slow and sullen and utterly uninterested in being moved, and the drovers have started charging a surcharge for the delay.
etl_dead.accept_text: They block the road and the carts. Eight, and drag them off the verge. If you can bury them, so much the better. If not, put them somewhere the wind can't reach.
etl_dead.turn_in_text: The road is clear. Now we can complain about something else. Choose what suits you. And thank the drovers for their patience, if you see them. They've been patient for months.

etl_remnants.description: South of the landing lie the Ruins of Lordaeron: the old capital, the gate to the Undercity, and a thousand remnants of men who never left. They snap at anyone who passes, and Linnea has lost three couriers to them since the first frost.
etl_remnants.accept_text: Go south, to the ruins. The remnants are tireless. Eight, and don't stand in the open. They remember being soldiers, and soldiers remember cover.
etl_remnants.turn_in_text: That will give the road a rest. Take what you need. They were good men, once. They deserve to be remembered better than they are.

etl_signets.description: The remnants wear the signet rings of the old court. Linnea wants them: not for the gold, but because some of them can still be traced to families who might want to know. It is the last courtesy she can offer the dead, and the only one she has the stomach for.
etl_signets.accept_text: Four signets. They're on the remnants. Treat them with a little respect. They were somebody's husband, somebody's father. Don't pry the rings off like a thief.
etl_signets.turn_in_text: Four. Each one a family. I'll send them word. Take something for your trouble. Some of those families will be glad. Some will not. All of them will have wanted to know.

etm_restless.description: Gravekeeper Morvyn tends Faol's Rest, the old pilgrims' graveyard. The dead there will not stay put. They claw up through the soil and stand in the rows, silent and patient, as though waiting for a service that never began.
etm_restless.accept_text: They wander the rows. Eight, and be gentle with the stones. Pilgrims came a long way to rest here, and I'd like their markers to still read.
etm_restless.turn_in_text: Back in the ground, or near enough. Thank you. Pick whatever you can use. I'll walk the rows tonight and say what words I can remember. It's all they ever asked.

etm_seals.description: Faol's grave was sealed by a ring of stone fragments, set by the pilgrims who buried him. The restless have been taking them one by one, and Morvyn does not know why. She wants them back before the seal fails entirely.
etm_seals.accept_text: The restless carry the fragments. Four will do it. Bring them to me. Don't drop one. They're older than this graveyard.
etm_seals.turn_in_text: The seal is mended. Mostly. Take something for the trouble. Faol was a strange saint, by all accounts. I think he'd have wanted to be left alone. I'll try to oblige.

etm_melrache.description: A Scarlet captain, Melrache, has made Faol's Rest his camp, digging up graves and calling it a crusade. Morvyn has watched him from the hill, and wants him made to understand that cemeteries are not battlefields, and that every dead person has someone who loved them.
etm_melrache.accept_text: He sits at the north end of the rows. Clear the restless, then him. He thinks he's cleansing the dead. Show him what cleansing really means.
etm_melrache.turn_in_text: Melrache's dead. Faol can rest. Take your pick of the camp. And thank you, for the graves. I'll tell the pilgrims, if any come. I think they would like it.

etg_wretches.description: Warden Gunther Lorn watches Brightwater Lake. The Drowned Wretches crawl out of it at dusk, moaning the names of the lost, and he knows every name by heart. He wants them back in the water, and wants the names to stop.
etg_wretches.accept_text: They come out at dusk. Eight, and keep your feet dry if you can. The names they moan are real. Try not to listen. I've listened for years, and I regret each one.
etg_wretches.turn_in_text: That's the shore quiet. Thanks. Have your choice of the lot. I'll stand a little longer on the pier tonight. It's the least I can do for those I didn't save.

etg_ice.description: The lake sheds black ice shards, and the shades hoard them. Gunther is convinced they are what is making the water cold, and that the cold is spreading. He'd like them gone, before the lake freezes in the middle of summer.
etg_ice.accept_text: The shades carry them. Five shards, and don't stand too long near the water. They draw the heat out of you without any fuss. I lost two fingers to them before I knew.
etg_ice.turn_in_text: Five. The lake will warm, I think. Slowly. Take something. I'll be glad to feel the sun on my hands again. Even dead hands remember warmth.

etg_bethor.description: Bethor Iceshard is a shade who has grown too cold to die. He stands at the centre of the lake and drains the warmth from anything near, and every night the ice around him creeps a little closer to the shore. Gunther would like it to stop creeping.
etg_bethor.accept_text: He stands where the ice is thickest. His shades guard him. Take them first. Wear everything you own, and don't let him speak. His voice is colder than his hands.
etg_bethor.turn_in_text: The lake is warming already. I can feel it. Choose well. I'll tell Ohmsted. He'll ring the bell for you. Don't flinch when he does. It's meant kindly.

eth_converts.description: Scout Hallam watches the Crusader Outpost east of Brill. The recruits there are loud, young, and entirely unprepared, and they are also a month away from being a real threat. Hallam would prefer to deal with them now, while they are still stupid.
eth_converts.accept_text: They train in the yard. Eight, and keep them from the road. If they chant, ignore them. They chant to build courage. It doesn't usually work.
eth_converts.turn_in_text: Fewer recruits, fewer problems. Take your pick. I'll watch the yard another week, and then I'll decide whether the Crusade is worth my time. I suspect it is.

eth_initiates.description: Behind the recruits come the Initiates: drilled, armed and fanatical. They guard the outpost's gate and its secrets, and they take turns on watch without complaint. Hallam finds it hard to hate such discipline, and harder to forgive.
eth_initiates.accept_text: Don't take more than two at a time. Six should give them pause. And watch for the ones with the bandaged hands. They pray with their fists.
eth_initiates.turn_in_text: Six. They'll be rattled. Take something from the supply. If you're hurt, come back to Brill. I know a woman who heals the unlucky.

eth_brennic.description: Crusader Brennic commands the outpost. He's strong, devout and utterly merciless, and Hallam has watched him order the execution of a boy who would not recite a creed. Without Brennic, the garrison will fall. With him, it will not.
eth_brennic.accept_text: He's in the tower. His recruits rally to him, so take them first. He doesn't stop for wounded and he doesn't stop for pleas. Neither should you.
eth_brennic.turn_in_text: Brennic's down. The outpost is leaderless. Choose what suits you. Remember what he was. Don't mistake mercy for weakness. Not out here.

etr_skitterers.description: Huntress Ravel tracks the spiders of Venomweb Vale. The skitterers breed faster than she can hunt them, and their bite paralyses. She has taken up a new hobby of calculating how long the Vale will last at their current rate, and the figure keeps shrinking.
etr_skitterers.accept_text: They hide in the webs. Eight, and watch for the big one. If the web is wet, it's recent. If it's dry, it's a trap. If it's both, run.
etr_skitterers.turn_in_text: The Vale is quieter. Thanks. Take something. I'll set my traps by the north spur tonight. If you want to see how it's done, come by.

etr_sacs.description: Venomweb venom is worth a fortune to the Apothecaries. Ravel wants five sacs: for the Undercity, for the war, and for her own reasons, which she does not elaborate on. She needs them whole, because broken sacs lose their potency in a day.
etr_sacs.accept_text: The skitterers and the night-webs carry them. Five, and don't pop them. A popped sac is a ruined sac. A ruined sac is a wasted spider.
etr_sacs.turn_in_text: Five sacs. A fine haul. Take your pick of the lot. I'll see they reach the Apothecary within the hour. You've done a sound piece of work, and I'll say it again if you like.

etr_mother.description: Mother Venomweb is the matriarch of the Vale: a huge spider, venom-fat and cunning. Every skitterer in the Vale is her brood, and every night she grows. Ravel wants her gone before the next spring, when the hatchlings would number in the thousands.
etr_mother.accept_text: She sits at the heart of the web. Her brood guards her. Take them first. Don't let her wrap you. She prefers them alive for a night, and she's patient about it.
etr_mother.turn_in_text: The Mother's dead. The Vale is yours. Take your pick of her hoard. I'll never forget the sound of the web when she fell. It sounded like a breath being let go.

etb_worgs.description: Stablehand Edric tends what remains of the Balnir farmstead. The Bleak Worgs have taken over the paddock and eat whatever stumbles in, which has recently included his dog. He is not a violent man, but he has begun to practise.
etb_worgs.accept_text: They hide in the hay. Eight, and keep to the fences. They know the barn better than I do. Don't follow them in. Let them come out.
etb_worgs.turn_in_text: That's the paddock clear. Take something from the tack. I'll plant something in the east corner. Something that grows. It's been a long time since there was anything green in this yard.

etb_stableboys.description: The stableboys never left the farm. They roam the paddock with pitchforks, loyal to a master who died long ago. Edric knew some of them. He wants them put to rest, and he wants it done by someone who will not laugh at the pitchforks.
etb_stableboys.accept_text: They don't know. Treat them kindly. Eight. If one of them asks for the master, tell him he's on his way. It's not a lie, strictly.
etb_stableboys.turn_in_text: They're at rest. Thank you. Pick whatever you can use. I'll mend the stable doors in the morning. They'd have liked that.

etb_vachon.description: Captain Vachon led the Balnir militia. He now leads the dead, a stubborn old soldier who refuses to give up the farm. He has stood the same post for years and has never once been relieved, and Edric thinks it is a miracle he has stayed so sharp.
etb_vachon.accept_text: He's at the farmhouse. His stableboys guard him. Take them first. He'll challenge you. Answer in the form of a salute, if you can.
etb_vachon.turn_in_text: Vachon's at peace. The farm is quiet. Have your choice of the lot. He was a good captain. I'll tell his sons, if I can find them, that he held until the end.

etd_acolytes.description: Warden Ysolde Grave watches the Cult of the Damned farm. Its acolytes call on powers no one should, in a cellar that smells of old cabbage and older blood, and the Undercity wants them silenced before they find a name for what they're calling.
etd_acolytes.accept_text: They chant in the cellar. Eight, and don't let them finish a verse. The verse ends with a name. If you hear the name, stop listening.
etd_acolytes.turn_in_text: That will quiet the cellar. Take something. I'll keep a watch on the door tonight. The cult will notice the quiet, and it will not like it.

etd_ledger.description: The cult keeps meticulous records: names, tallies, debts. The pages are scattered on the bodies of its members, and Ysolde wants them for the Undercity, to learn who has been paying the cult's bills, and who has been collecting.
etd_ledger.accept_text: The acolytes and the fanatics carry them. Five pages, and don't read them aloud. Some of the names are living. Some of those names are in places I'd rather not say.
etd_ledger.turn_in_text: Five pages. Enough for a warrant. Choose well. I'll have them carried to the Undercity by an honest hand. You've done more than you know.

etd_thaddeus.description: Overseer Thaddeus leads the cult. He sits in the farm's deepest cellar, issuing orders to the damned in a voice like wet cloth. His death would unravel the lot, and Ysolde has been waiting for the right hand to unravel it.
etd_thaddeus.accept_text: He's in the cellar. His fanatics guard the stairs. Take them first. He smiles when he's angry. Don't let him smile at you.
etd_thaddeus.turn_in_text: The cult is leaderless. Excellent. Take your pick of his robes. I'll burn the rest. A cult's best friend is a tidy collection of robes.

ets_bowmen.description: Scout Hollowmere watches the Scarlet Watch Post from the lakeside slope. Their bowmen patrol the north coast road and pick off anyone who passes, Forsaken or otherwise, and Hollowmere has the arrow-wounds to prove they are not particular.
ets_bowmen.accept_text: Stay low. They shoot first. Eight, and watch the shadows. If you see the flash of a quiver, you're already in range.
ets_bowmen.turn_in_text: That's the road open. Thank you. Take something. It's good to walk a road without feeling the weight of a bowstring on my back.

ets_zealots.description: The Watch Post is held by zealots, who preach as they fight. They shout scripture at the dead, and the dead, being polite, do not answer. Hollowmere would like them to stop preaching, mostly because it is wearing on the nerves.
ets_zealots.accept_text: They don't stop. Eight, and keep your ears covered. I stuffed mine with wax last time. It still wasn't enough.
ets_zealots.turn_in_text: Quieter. For a while. Take your pick. I'll enjoy the silence while it lasts. It won't last, but I'll enjoy it.

ets_preachers.description: The preachers are the worst of them. They call down fire on the faithless, and in the Scarlet Crusade's reckoning, that includes everyone who is not Scarlet. Hollowmere has the burn scars to prove it, and will not be argued with on the subject.
ets_preachers.accept_text: They stand on the steps and burn things. Six, and don't stand in the fire. They'll aim for the ones who run, so don't run.
ets_preachers.turn_in_text: Six sermons ended. Thank you. Take something. I wish I could say the fire is finished, but I've learned not to say such things aloud.

ets_vishas.description: Interrogator Vishas runs the Watch Post's cells. He's patient, methodical and cruel, and Hollowmere knows what he does to prisoners because Hollowmere was one. He wants Vishas dead, and the cells emptied, and has no interest in forgiveness.
ets_vishas.accept_text: He's in the cells. His zealots guard the door. Take them first. He will talk to you, calmly, and reasonably. He is lying. He has always been lying.
ets_vishas.turn_in_text: Vishas is dead. The cells are open. Choose what suits you. I'll walk the corridor tomorrow and say a few things to the walls. It's been owed.

brl_dispatch.description: Rennick doesn't trust the Faol's Rest gravekeeper's reports to arrive on their own, and he doesn't trust his own messenger boys to arrive at all. A sealed dispatch must reach Gravekeeper Morvyn, over the hills in the east, and he would like it carried by someone who will not stop for conversation.
brl_dispatch.accept_text: Eastern Tirisfal, the graveyard on the hill at Faol's Rest. Put it in her hand, not on her desk. Don't read it. Don't linger. And if the dead are restless, go around them, not through.
brl_dispatch.turn_in_text: Rennick's seal. Hm. He worries so loudly for a man who never leaves the square. Here, for the road. And tell him next time to send a flag instead of a letter. I'll understand it better.

brl_guard_smelt.description: The gate guard's kit is falling apart, and Brill's new forge by the east market is going unused. Nobody has had the nerve to light it. Smelt two copper bars from Tirisfal ore and he will show you what they are for, and what a forge is, if you need reminding.
brl_guard_smelt.accept_text: Copper ore is in the hills. Smelt two bars at the forge past the market and bring them. I'll supply the nagging. And don't burn the bellows. I paid for those.
brl_guard_smelt.turn_in_text: Two bars. Clean, too. Let's make something of them. You've got the knack. Most people let the slag in. You didn't.

brl_guard_bracers.description: A pair of copper bracers, forged by your own hands at the Brill forge. The guard wants proof the forge works before he trusts it with his armour, and he has decided that you are the proof.
brl_guard_bracers.accept_text: Two bars, a hammer and some patience. Make the bracers. Mind the sparks. And don't hurry. A hurried bracer is a hurried grave, and I'd like to wear these a while.
brl_guard_bracers.turn_in_text: Crooked, but sturdy. I'll wear them proudly. Here's something for your trouble. And if anyone laughs at the crooked, tell them it was a veteran's design.

brl_locket.description: A tarnished locket, found on one of the wandering dead. The portrait inside is almost gone, but the inscription on the back is plain enough: "For Marren, from Aldric". The widow Marren lives at the Solliden Farmstead, and you suspect she has been waiting a long time.
brl_locket.accept_text: You turn the locket over. The clasp has rusted shut, but the inscription is legible. Marren, at the Solliden fields. You should take it to her.
brl_locket.turn_in_text: Marren turns it over and over in her hands. "Aldric." She says nothing else for a while. Then: "Thank you. Take this." Her voice is steady, but her hands are not.

ets_bowman_orders.description: Scarlet Crusade orders, torn from a bowman's quiver: troop positions, patrol times, and a map of the north coast. Deathguard Rennick will want these in Brill, and he will want them quickly, before the Crusade changes its watch.
ets_bowman_orders.accept_text: You skim the orders. Troop positions, patrol times, a route along the coast. This belongs with Rennick in Brill. Don't dally. A change of watch is a change of plan.
ets_bowman_orders.turn_in_text: Rennick reads it twice and swears quietly. "Their patrols run to the hour. Good. This is worth a great deal." He folds it into his coat as if it were a letter from home.

etd_ledger_courier.description: Ysolde has bound the cult's ledger pages into a bundle and wants it in the hands of someone who can read the cipher. The one she trusts is Keeper Oswin at Raven Hill Cemetery in Silverpine North, through the pass to the north-west, and she does not trust anyone else to carry it.
etd_ledger_courier.accept_text: The portal at the edge of the Landing leads into Silverpine. Raven Hill Cemetery, Keeper Oswin. Don't let anyone read it. Don't let anyone ask what it is. If someone follows you, drop it and run.
etd_ledger_courier.turn_in_text: Oswin turns the bundle over, and his face changes. "The Agamand seal. Of course. Come back when you've seen their house." He folds it away without another word, and stares at the wall.

sp_ledger_cipher.description: Oswin can read the cult's ledger, but only half of it. The cipher keys are the Agamand family seals, and only someone who has stood in the Agamand mansion could match them. He needs the husks behind Raven Hill thinned first, so the dead stop interrupting his reading.
sp_ledger_cipher.accept_text: You've been through the Agamand house, and you carried the ledger here. Good. Now clear the husks at Raven Hill so I can read in peace. They don't know when to stop knocking.
sp_ledger_cipher.turn_in_text: Eight husks, and the seals match. The ledger names the cult's patrons. Silverpine will want to hear this. Pick whatever you can use. I'll send word south. Quietly. The names are in places that listen.

etc_descend.description: The Cult of the Damned dug their cellar into something that was never meant to be dug: the bones of a Scourge Abomination, so large its spine is a corridor. Boneward Calder wants to know how far the passage runs before anyone commits to it.
etc_descend.accept_text: The cave mouth is behind the cult's farm. Walk the spine to the middle of the ribs and come back. Don't pick anything up. Don't touch the walls. They remember.
etc_descend.turn_in_text: So it runs that far. Right. Then the rest is a matter of killing what lives in the ribs. Good work. Don't tell me what you saw. I'd rather not know until I have to.

etc_warriors.description: Scourge Warriors wander the rib tunnels in loose patrols. They don't sleep, they don't tire, and they are very bad at hiding, which has been the only mercy of the whole business. Calder wants the first ranks thinned before the cult learns to use them.
etc_warriors.accept_text: Eight of them. Fight in the tunnels, not the open hall, and let them come to you. They march in step. If you break the step, they stumble.
etc_warriors.turn_in_text: Eight fewer. The ribs sound quieter already. Take something. I'd say rest, but the next room has teeth.

etc_ghouls.description: The ghouls came with the Scourge, but they stayed for the plague cellar. They are fast, they travel in packs, and they hunt by the sound of a heartbeat, which has made Calder's last three patrols very short.
etc_ghouls.accept_text: They hunt by the sound of heartbeats, which makes you a very noisy guest. Eight. Move slowly, breathe shallowly, and don't whistle.
etc_ghouls.turn_in_text: Eight ghouls. Do you still have all your fingers? Good. Have your choice of the lot. I've seen worse. Not often, though.

etc_runes.description: The Scourge Necromancers carve their wards onto black shards of stone, and the same wards hold the Abomination's bones in place. Calder wants a handful, to learn how to break them. He has a theory, and it needs hardware.
etc_runes.accept_text: The necromancers carry them. Six shards, uncracked. Don't read the runes aloud. They're not hard to say. That's what's wrong with them.
etc_runes.turn_in_text: Six clean shards. Now I can see where the wards sit. The Abomination is next. Choose well. I'll study these tonight. Don't expect me to be good company.

etc_abomination.description: The Abomination sits in the skull at the head of the spine, wired into the cult's rune stones. It has been dead for a very long time, and has only recently begun to wake. Kill it, and the cellar is just a cellar again.
etc_abomination.accept_text: The skull throne, at the north end of the spine. Necromancers keep it standing. Take them first. If it starts to hum, leave. If it starts to sing, run.
etc_abomination.turn_in_text: It's down. The cellar is quiet. I'll be sleeping with a candle on for a week. Take your pick of what it wore. I'd keep it, if I were you. Not for the loot. For the story.

etc_krag.description: Ghoulmaster Krag keeps his pack in a bone-lined pit west of the ribs. He feeds them on what the cult leaves behind, and he has a way of whistling that makes the walls tremble. Calder would like the whistle stopped.
etc_krag.accept_text: West of the second rib, down a side tunnel. He whistles for the pack when he's losing. Be quick. And don't hum along. Some of them know the tune.
etc_krag.turn_in_text: Krag's whistle is silent. Take your pick of his trophies. I'm told they're tooth-shaped. I'm not going to check.

etc_orvyn.description: Plaguemaster Orvyn runs the cult's laboratory in a side chamber east of the ribs, brewing the blight they pour on the farms above. Calder wants the vats cold, and has wanted it for a very long time.
etc_orvyn.accept_text: East of the third rib, past a tunnel of vials. His acolytes tend the vats. Keep your mouth covered. I've seen what happens to those who don't.
etc_orvyn.turn_in_text: The vats are cold. Whatever he was brewing, it won't reach the farms. Take your pick. And please, wash. Twice. Then burn the clothes.

etc_formula.description: A sheaf of stained notes pulled from the Plaguemaster's belt: dosages, ingredients, and a diagram of the cult's delivery vats. Assistant Grael at the Brill Apothecary would pay dearly for this, and would probably keep the pages for himself.
etc_formula.accept_text: The handwriting is clinical. Every line ends in the same instruction: "dilute before use". Take it to Grael, at Brill's apothecary. He'll know what it means. He may wish he didn't.
etc_formula.turn_in_text: Grael reads it twice and goes slightly pale. "They were going to put this in the wells. Thank you. Truly." He puts the pages down very carefully, as though they might bite.
